branch: Phase III branch 1/2 — Habitat suitability (PU-learning + GAM + confounding audit)

pu_setup.label_state: positive (n=597) vs two INDEPENDENT background sets, never merged
pu_setup.model_b_randombg: background = ctrl_random_bg (n=20000, 19 overlap with positive kept as positive); presence+bg pool n=20578
pu_setup.why_two_models: target-group background (Phillips et al. 2009) matches the survey-effort distribution of the presence records more closely than a spatially uniform random background, so comparing the two isolates how much of any apparent signal is driven by effort matching vs raw geography.

pu_correction_method: LightGBM binary classifier with scale_pos_weight = n_background/n_presence per model (29.9 for target-group bg, 43.1 for random bg) to counter the presence/background class imbalance at training time. On top of that we apply an Elkan-Noto (2008) style single-constant correction: the label frequency c = P(labeled=1 | y=1) is estimated by 5-fold out-of-fold cross-validation on the training positives (mean predicted probability of held-out positives), giving c_hat_targetbg=0.7256 and c_hat_randombg=0.9709; the true positive-class posterior is then estimated as f_calibrated(x) = min(f(x)/c_hat, 1). Raw and calibrated scores are both stored in suitability_predictions.parquet; the calibrated column is the one that approximates P(species present | x) under the PU 'selected completely at random' assumption, while the raw column is P(labeled positive | x), the quantity LightGBM directly optimizes.

spatial_holdout.method: hold out 7 whole oblasts (never used in training) purely for this diagnostic step; full spatial block CV is done by the separate Validation branch

model_performance.interpretation: The random-background model scores much higher (AUC 0.998, AP 0.933) than the target-group model (AUC 0.968, AP 0.605) purely because random background cells are drawn from the whole country and are trivially separable from presence cells on effort/access features alone (most of Ukraine was never surveyed for Apiaceae at all). The target-group model is the methodologically preferred estimate because its background is drawn from the same effort distribution as the presence records, so its lower, more modest AP is a more honest estimate of habitat separability net of survey bias.

gam_step.algorithm: pyGAM LogisticGAM, natural cubic splines (n_splines=12, lam=0.6) per term
gam_step.training_data: positive cells (n=377, all years) + a 5x random subsample of target-group background from the same non-holdout oblasts (n=1885) — full-imbalance weighting caused PIRLS divergence, so a balanced subsample was used for GAM fitting only (LightGBM PU model above still uses the full data with scale_pos_weight)

non_smooth_boundary_check.method: within each dist_road_m octile (holding road-distance roughly fixed), computed presence-rate variance across oblasts with >=20 observations in that bin
non_smooth_boundary_check.result: presence rate varies by up to 0.28 (absolute) across oblasts within the same road-distance bin, and this range does not shrink monotonically with distance from road — evidence that observed spatial pattern is not fully described by smooth environmental gradients and instead reflects oblast-level differences in survey intensity that the PDP (a national marginal average) cannot show
non_smooth_boundary_check.conclusion: no sharp single-point discontinuity was found exactly at the ~50km MERRA-2 support boundary or the WorldClim nodata-fill boundary in the plotted range, but the oblast-level rate heterogeneity documented above is a real non-smoothness the PDP curve cannot expose because it marginalizes over oblast

ablation_result.interpretation: Removing the 13 effort/dist_road features costs only 0.005 AUC and 0.040 AP (0.605->0.565) — a small, measurable but not dominant loss. The much larger driver of holdout AP is river-connectivity to already-known patches: the ablation group labeled 'no_river_connectivity' removes 4 features (n_upstream_target_patches_50km, network_distance_to_nearest_infected_km, has_upstream_infection_50km, AND ord_stra, the Strahler stream order of the nearest reach) and collapses AP from 0.605 to 0.140. A follow-up isolation test (see isolation_of_ord_stra below) shows ord_stra alone contributes essentially nothing (AP actually rises slightly to 0.608 when only ord_stra is removed), while removing only the other 3 named features reproduces almost the entire collapse (AP 0.605->0.145) -- so the ~77% relative AP loss is correctly attributed to the 3 known-patch-connectivity features specifically, not to ord_stra. This is expected and is itself a confound of a different kind: those features encode 'is this reach near an already-detected population', which is partly biology (spread follows rivers) and partly detection history (a patch is 'known' only where it was surveyed) -- removing both effort/dist_road AND all 4 river-connectivity-group features together drops performance to AUC 0.675 / AP 0.134, only marginally below removing the connectivity group alone, confirming known-patch connectivity is the dominant confound/signal source, with effort/dist_road as a smaller but real secondary one.

isolation_of_ord_stra.purpose: the no_river_connectivity ablation group above bundles 4 features (n_upstream_target_patches_50km, network_distance_to_nearest_infected_km, has_upstream_infection_50km, ord_stra); this isolation test disentangles ord_stra's own contribution from the other three
isolation_of_ord_stra.conclusion: removing ord_stra alone barely moves AP (0.605->0.608, a negligible +0.003), while removing only the 3 named known-patch-connectivity features reproduces almost the full collapse (0.605->0.145, vs 0.140 when all 4 are removed together) -- confirming the ~77% AP loss is attributable to the 3 named features, not to ord_stra, which was bundled into the ablation group but does not independently drive the effect.

shap_dist_road_stratification.method: SHAP TreeExplainer on spatial holdout (7 oblasts, n=3009); dist_road_m values split into quintiles
shap_dist_road_stratification.what_this_confirms: The SHAP effect of dist_road_m is non-monotonic across distance quintiles (positive near road, negative mid-range, positive again far from road) rather than a clean monotonic 'closer-to-road-is-more-suitable' biological signal. There is a small but statistically significant positive Spearman correlation (rho=0.053, p=0.0037) between the dist_road_m SHAP value and 5km plant-effort counts on the holdout, meaning part of what dist_road_m contributes to the model overlaps with what the effort buffer already explains.
shap_dist_road_stratification.what_this_does_not_prove: This does NOT prove dist_road_m carries zero biological information (habitat near roads genuinely differs: more disturbed, warmer microclimate, more propagule pressure from vehicle-mediated seed dispersal -- a documented real invasion pathway for Heracleum sosnowskyi). The correlation with effort is moderate (|rho|<0.15 throughout this project), not total collinearity, so dist_road_m is a mixed signal, not a pure effort proxy -- it should be interpreted with that caveat, not dropped outright nor trusted as clean.

confounding_conclusion: Effort/access features (dist_road_m + the 12 buffer counts) explain a real but modest slice of predictive performance on the spatial holdout (AP drops 0.605->0.565, -6.6% relative, when removed), confirming the slides-24/25/57 trap is present but not catastrophic for this feature set once effort buffers are included as explicit controls per the project's own design. The larger confound in this model is river-network connectivity to already-detected patches: removing the 3 named connectivity features (n_upstream_target_patches_50km, network_distance_to_nearest_infected_km, has_upstream_infection_50km) alone drops AP to 0.145, confirmed by an isolation test to be attributable to these 3 features specifically and not to ord_stra (Strahler stream order), which was also removed in the same ablation group for convenience but independently contributes nothing (AP 0.608 when removed alone). This connectivity signal genuinely mixes real biological spread-along-rivers with detection history (a patch can only be 'known infected' where surveyors looked), and current data cannot cleanly separate the two. dist_road_m's SHAP contribution is non-monotonic across distance and weakly but significantly correlated with 5km effort counts, so it should be read as a mixed accessibility/biology signal, not a clean remoteness covariate -- consistent with the multicollinearity warning already logged in the Phase III feature manifest.
limitations: Zero verified_negative labels exist anywhere in this dataset; all reported AUC/AP compare presence against pseudo-background, not against confirmed absence.
Only 597 positive cells nationally and 220 in the 7-oblast spatial holdout; AP estimates on this holdout have wide sampling uncertainty and should not be read to 3 significant figures.

The random-background model's very high AUC/AP (0.998/0.933) is an artifact of comparing surveyed vs never-surveyed geography, not a better habitat model -- the target-group model is the methodologically preferred comparison.

This holdout (7 oblasts, chosen to keep ~19% of cells and ~37% of positives) is a diagnostic split for this branch only; the separate spatial block CV in the Validation branch is the authoritative generalization estimate.

River-connectivity features (n_upstream_target_patches_50km, network_distance_to_nearest_infected_km, has_upstream_infection_50km) dominate both permutation importance and SHAP; they encode 'near a known patch', which mixes true riverine spread with detection history and cannot be disentangled with the data on hand.

GAM was fit on a balanced subsample (all positives + 5x random target-group background) because the full-imbalance weighted fit diverged in PIRLS; the LightGBM PU models used for predictions and ablation still use the full presence/background pool with scale_pos_weight.

Elkan-Noto c_hat differs substantially between the two background choices (0.73 target-group vs 0.97 random-bg), reflecting that target-group background cells are much harder to distinguish from presence than random background cells -- as expected since they share the same survey-effort distribution.

Climate/wind features carry ~50 km spatial support (median 2467 one-km cells share one value) and WorldClim/terrain carry ~3-4.6 km support; neither is a true 1 km local measurement, a caveat inherited unchanged from the Phase III feature-table manifest.
dist_road_m is built from Natural Earth roads covering only ~19% of Ukraine's true road length (major/trunk roads only); it is a distance-to-major-road proxy, not distance to any road.

The 'no_river_connectivity' ablation group bundles 4 features, not 3: ord_stra (Strahler stream order of the nearest reach) was included alongside the 3 known-patch-connectivity features for convenience; an isolation test (ablation_result.isolation_of_ord_stra) confirms ord_stra's own contribution to holdout AP is negligible (+0.003 when removed alone), so the reported 77% AP loss is correctly attributed to the other 3 features.
notes_for_next_phase: suitability_predictions.parquet provides suitability_targetbg / suitability_randombg (calibrated, PU-corrected) and ensemble_mean/ensemble_std for every one of the 599126 cells, keyed on cell_id -- this is the TODO-placeholder input the parallel Spread-risk branch is waiting on. Use suitability_targetbg as the primary habitat layer (methodologically preferred background) and ensemble_std as a simple two-model disagreement/uncertainty proxy; a proper spatial-CV-based uncertainty estimate should come from the Validation branch, not this single train/holdout split.
